answer: An agent economy can make influence proportional to a scarce, slashable stake: each identity must lock tokens before it can vote on a trade or claim a shared reward, and fraud proven by conflicting signed actions burns that stake. Splitting funds across a thousand identities does not multiply voting weight; it only fragments the same capital and exposes each deposit to loss. Like nectar guarded in a garden, access is earned, not created by adding names; a sable attacker must tie up real value and risk forfeiting it.
